Goa imports most of its electricity from central generating stations and
other states. The state has little land for large solar parks, and wind
speeds along the coast are low for much of the year. India's national
targets therefore weigh heavily on a small state with few options.
The government has proposed rooftop solar, floating solar on reservoirs
and battery storage as the main local resources.

The cost of these options has fallen sharply since 2015. Rooftop systems
now cost about half what they did then, and battery prices have dropped
by more than 80 per cent. Goa can therefore plan for a much larger share
of local generation than it could a decade ago.
